limits: A stipulated atmosphere, not weather observations.
All three formulas apply lapse directly to the argument: it is effectively geopotential height. The JS interface says metres MSL and does not convert geometric height.

At geometric 2500 m the source gives H=2499 m and T=271.906 K. Passing 2500 directly yields the geopotential temperature; geometric use slightly understates temperature, pressure and density. The rounded Z column is not a conversion algorithm.
historical_comparison.interpretation: All three project ISA implementations are evaluated at the five Table I geopotential heights. Their independent agreement with the printed table is distinct from their mutual agreement: the table below retains all three values. The JS constant R=287.0528 differs from the Python value 287.05. None converts geometric height.

source_table_records.quantity: sea-level temperature, pressure and density at geopotential altitude 0 m
source_table_records.conditions: U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976, Table I, geopotential altitude, metric units. Argument is geopotential height H, not geometric height Z. Pressure is a five-digit mantissa times a power of ten, in millibar. The same row's P0 in the constants section is 1.013250 × 10^5 Pa, so 1 mb = 100 Pa in this document.
source_table_records.locator: Table I, Geopotential Altitude, Metric Units, document page 52. In the NTRS scan, document page = PDF page minus 16 (PDF page 67).
source_table_records.limits: This is the defining model atmosphere, not a measured profile. A density function is checked against these printed digits. Four significant figures of density at this row are 1.225 kg/m^3.

source_table_records.quantity: temperature, pressure and density at geopotential altitude 1000 m
source_table_records.conditions: Same table and column definitions as the sea-level row. Z is printed as 1000 m.
source_table_records.limits: Publish the printed mantissa. Four significant figures of density are 1.112 kg/m^3. Do not replace the table with the recomputed last pressure digit.

source_table_records.quantity: temperature, pressure and density at geopotential altitude 2000 m
source_table_records.conditions: Same geopotential table. Geometric height on this row is 2001 m, not 2000 m.
source_table_records.limits: Four significant figures of density are 1.006 or 1.007 depending on rounding of 1.0065; the printed value is 1.0065. Use H, not Z, as the argument.

source_table_records.quantity: temperature, pressure and density at geopotential altitude 2500 m
source_table_records.conditions: Same geopotential table, document page 52. This is not the geometric-altitude row on document page 53, where Z = 2500 m has H = 2499 m, T = 271.906 K and a different pressure.
source_table_records.locator: Table I, geopotential, document page 52, row H = 2500
source_table_records.limits: Do not take the page-53 geometric row. Four significant figures of density are 0.9569 kg/m^3.

source_table_records.quantity: temperature, pressure and density at geopotential altitude 3000 m
source_table_records.conditions: Continuation of the geopotential table. Document page 54, not page 53.
source_table_records.locator: Table I, Geopotential Altitude, Metric Units, document page 54 (NTRS PDF page 69)
source_table_records.limits: Four significant figures of density are 0.9091 kg/m^3. The printed pressure mantissa is 7.0108, the truncation of 701.085.

source_table_records.quantity: universal gas constant R-star, prose value
source_table_records.conditions: Adopted constant of the 1976 standard. The prose says this value is consistent with the carbon-12 scale and is the value used in the 1962 Standard, and is not exactly consistent with the cited k and N_A.
source_table_records.locator: Document page 3, section Defining Constants and Equations, symbol R*
source_table_records.limits: Table 2 on document page 2 prints R* as 8.31432 × 10^-3 in the same unit. That exponent is a typesetting error. Use the page-3 prose.

source_table_records.conditions: Table 2, Category I, as printed. Disagrees with the page-3 prose by a factor of 10^6.
source_table_records.limits: Recorded so it is not silently corrected. A model that uses this printed exponent will miss the Table I densities by orders of magnitude. The adopted value is the page-3 prose.

source_table_records.quantity: sea-level pressure P0, sea-level temperature T0, and g0
source_table_records.conditions: Adopted constants. g0 is the sea-level standard acceleration of gravity. g0' is defined so that one standard geopotential metre corresponds numerically to lifting one kilogram through one metre at 9.80665 J.
source_table_records.locator: P0 and g0 prose, document page 3; T0 and g0' also in Table 2, document page 2, and T0 is the H = 0 temperature in Table I
source_table_records.limits: Table 2 also prints r0 as 6.356766 × 10^6 km and sigma as 3.65 × 10^-1 m. Those two units or exponents are inconsistent with a terrestrial radius and a molecular diameter. They are not needed to check density against Table I. Sutherland's S = 110 K is printed in Table 2 and is a viscosity constant, not a density constant.

source_table_records.conditions: Lowest layer of the defined temperature-height profile, from the surface to 11 geopotential kilometres. Temperature in this layer is linear in geopotential height.
source_table_records.locator: Table 4, document page 3, row b = 0, and the following row b = 1 at 11 km'
source_table_records.limits: The gradient is per standard geopotential kilometre. It does not apply above 11 km'.

source_table_records.quantity: molecular weights of helium and hydrogen as constituents of dry air, and the geopotential definition
source_table_records.conditions: Table 3 is the composition of sea-level dry air, not the molar mass of a pure lifting gas. The fractional volumes are trace abundances.
source_table_records.locator: Table 3, document page 3. Equation (18), relating geopotential H to geometric Z, was read on its page image: H = (g0/g0') · (r0·Z)/(r0+Z).
source_table_records.limits: Do not use the helium fractional volume as a purity. The dry-air mean molar mass that recovers the sea-level density from P0, T0 and the prose R* is 28.9644 kg/kmol. That sentence was not re-opened on a page image in the final pass, so it is not given a page quote here. Table I, not a recomputed molar mass, is the check.
